description: The Canadian Payment Methods and Trends report is Payments Canada's annual study of how Canadian consumers and businesses pay, giving the volume and value of payment transactions by method: cash, cheques and paper, debit, credit and prepaid cards, contactless payments, electronic funds transfers, online transfers and international payments, with chapters on e-commerce, digital currencies and business payments. It is produced by Payments Canada, which owns and operates Canada's clearing and settlement systems, with data and input from the Bank of Canada, Statistics Canada, Interac, Euromonitor International and survey firms. Coverage is national; the 2025 edition, the twelfth, reports 12.2 trillion Canadian dollars in payment transactions, with annual totals, averages and one-, five- and ten-year growth rates to base year 2024 in its appendix charts. It is a free PDF. Caveats: figures combine operator data, third-party data and estimates described in the methodology appendix, only charts and tables in the PDF are given, not machine-readable files, and no reuse licence is stated. For simulation it provides the baseline mix and volume of payments that outage and cyber scenarios for card networks, transfer systems or the coming Real-Time Rail would disrupt, useful in resilience and capacity planning of financial infrastructure. It is related to the Reserve Bank of Australia payments data record in this catalogue, a comparable national series.
